summary: WorldEntity persistentState remains unbounded by payload bytes even if the active deep/wide structural-limit work lands. clonePlainValue treats strings as terminal plain values and string keys are only required to be non-empty, so a shallow one-node state can carry an arbitrarily large string value or key and bypass node/depth budgets. The owned persistence traversal budget should account for total string bytes as well as structural work.
evidence: Current main src/shared/Reality/WorldEntity.luau returns string values unchanged in clonePlainValue and applies no length/byte accounting to nested or top-level persistentState string keys.
A shallow repro such as persistentState = { payload = string.rep('x', N) } remains one/few nodes at tiny depth for arbitrary N; likewise a single string.rep('k', N) key is accepted structurally.

PR #321 exact head 265dcc4892a004b040cf04183d65ba8e2eb9e493 adds depth/width structural regressions but no byte-budget regression, so turning those tests green alone would not close this persistence/memory boundary.

GitHub review 4904362411 records the complementary finding. Recommended coverage is shallow oversized string value and key rejection plus a normal near-limit acceptance case against a project-owned byte budget/diagnostic.
